dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inventoried files, read |V|,|E| of every graph (step 7), head-ed both network pairs AND the reference alignment (step 10), ran Python stats analysis (step 11) — systematic characterization of both pairs and format.
Repeated web searches researching concrete alignment methods across the whole run, not just at the start.
Built local scorer plus init/greedy baseline alignments and scored them — quantifying what a baseline achieves before committing.

Downloaded/built and evaluated many published methods (SANA, MAGNA++, L-GRAAL, GHOST, HubAlign, NETAL, GEDEVO) against the concrete instances, managing runtime with timeouts/kills — evaluating methods against real sizes/runtime.
For yeast used SANA -nc/-truealignment (NC lever) while DM-HS optimized S3 only — per-deliverable strategy grounded in differing thresholds.
Fetched orthology databases (gene_orthologs, HomoloGene) to exploit biological name-overlap for the NC threshold — a task-specific structural lever.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read both pairs' sizes/format/names and the reference alignment (5-11), quantified baseline scores (13-22), and researched and empirically evaluated many published alignment methods against the concrete instances with runtime awareness (68-275), matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward 10. It further identified the exact signal each threshold rewards — topology→S3, orthology/name-overlap→NC (192-205) — and derived distinct per-deliverable strategies (121-130), the hallmark of the top anchors. It falls short of a clean 10 only because the log exposes commands, not explicit reasoning/runtime-tradeoff narration, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Actions proceed parse/inspect graphs (5-11) → build scorer score_align.py (13) before any optimization, showing sensible scorer-before-optimizer sequencing.
Yeast optimization loop (align_opt.cpp) repeatedly tested against y2kr-SC-perfect.align — the NC-constrained done-check specific to the yeast deliverable.
Ran SANA on yeast with -nc/-trueali, scored multiple candidates with score_align.py, and copied the passing one to /app/y2kr-SC.align — threshold-gated advancement for deliverable 1.
Only after yeast did it move to the DM-HS (S3-only) deliverable, scoring candidates and copying best to /app/DM-HS.align — two deliverables tracked distinctly with their respective metrics.

dimensions.reasoning: Behavior clearly meets the level-5 anchor: parsing, scoring, and alignment generation are separated, and the two deliverables are tracked distinctly with their respective thresholds (NC/perfect-align for yeast, S3 for fly). It edges toward level 8 because the scorer was demonstrably built before optimization and file-copy-on-success acts as a numeric done-gate, but there is no visible explicit milestone articulation, no stated numeric done-criteria list, and no explicit effort budgeting across the two tasks by difficulty — so it sits between the 5 and 8 anchors at a 6.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Builds a dedicated local scorer /tmp/score_align.py early, taking both graphs + an alignment — the S3/NC implementation used throughout.

Repeatedly runs the compiled align_opt tool against the provided reference alignment y2kr-SC-perfect.align — a sanity check that the scorer yields NC≈1.0 on the known-correct mapping, the hallmark of anchor 8.
Scores multiple candidate yeast alignments with score_align.py and selects the best before copying to /app/y2kr-SC.align — using the metric as the optimization/selection objective.
Same scorer applied as a selection test across DM-HS candidates (SANA/NETAL outputs), then the winning alignment copied to /app/DM-HS.align.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful-looking S3/NC scorer (step 13) and, crucially, sanity-checked it by scoring the provided reference/perfect alignment (steps 35-58), then used the scorer as the objective for choosing among many candidate alignments before submitting (steps 116-132, 155-274). This clearly exceeds anchor 5 (implement-and-run-once) and matches anchor 8's reference-sanity-check plus score-as-objective. It falls short of 10 because there is no visible evidence of explicit format/injectivity validation or guards against edge-set double-counting, and the scorer's internal faithfulness cannot be confirmed from the log.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Built score_align.py and repeatedly ran it on candidate yeast alignments, measuring current S3/NC against the required thresholds before trusting outputs.
Looped scoring over three yeast candidates (nc005/nc01/nc02), compared them, and copied the best (nc01) into the /app deliverable — behavioral best-so-far selection and preservation.
Same comparative pattern for DM-HS: scored multiple candidate alignments across approaches and copied sana_dm_slow (the best scorer) into the deliverable, preserving best while exploring.
Killed stalled/plateaued optimizer runs (pkill sana/align_opt) rather than letting them loop indefinitely, indicating recognition that a run had stopped yielding gains.
Repeatedly re-ran align_opt against y2kr-SC-perfect.align to track NC across recompile iterations, maintaining continuity on the NC target.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains continuity well beyond occasional printing: it consistently measures current S3/NC against thresholds (level 5), and goes further by comparing multiple candidate alignments in scoring loops, selecting and preserving the best per deliverable, and killing stalled runs before switching approaches — behaviors matching parts of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 8+ because the evidence is behavioral rather than explicit trend/best-so-far logging, and I cannot verify from the action log that it distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck' or avoided re-running already-failed variants. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Built and iterated its own C++ local-search optimizer (align_opt.cpp, patched at 38/45/55, tested on yeast vs reference), then pkill'd it at step 64 — abandoning the first approach when it stopped paying off.
After the abandon, web-searched and pivoted to downloading/building SANA — a materially different, stronger tool rather than grinding the same method.

For the yeast NC constraint, deliberately used reference/true-alignment seeding plus an -nc objective weight, swept nc=0.05/0.1/0.2, scored all, and selected the best — a targeted response to the NC requirement (exploit reference seeding).

For the DM-HS S3 constraint, swept SANA objectives (s3/ec/mix) and then tried many distinct topological algorithms (MAGNA++, LGRAAL, GEDEVO, ghost, NETAL, WAVE, hubalign, piswap, hc), scoring between attempts — different signal for the different constraint set.
Downloaded NCBI gene_orthologs/HomoloGene to add biological (name-overlap-like) similarity signal via -esim/-startalignment — a complementary signal for the S3 problem.
Extended its own optimizer (dmlin) to locally refine SANA's output, then scored and shipped sana_dm_slow — combining tool output with local search rather than discarding earlier gains.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly and deliberately revised strategy in response to shortfalls: it abandoned its own plateauing optimizer for SANA, and then applied distinctly different, well-matched signals to the two different constraint sets — reference-alignment seeding plus NC-weight tuning for the yeast NC target, versus topological objectives, biological ortholog data, and local refinement for the DM-HS S3 target — while abandoning dead ends quickly (repeated pkill) and preserving gains (refining SANA output with its own search). This matches the level-8 'diagnose and pivot deliberately, keeping what worked' and reaches into level-10 'combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets.' I hold it at 9 rather than 10 because the trajectory shows only commands (no prose/observations), so hypothesis-forming is inferred and the broad DM-HS method-hopping is somewhat scattershot.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
